text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Right-wing Disy party vice-president Nicos Anastassiades says senior civil servants who support communist Akel were undermining the government's work during the municipal elections campaign.
- Britain is pushing forward with a proposal for the deployment of a 5,000-strong multinational force on the island.
- Political terrorism. Anastassiades's report on the outcome of the municipal elections causes a storm of protest from all political parties.
- Two Britons are arrested for stealing confidential documents on pharmaceutical manufacturing.
- Disy is heading towards a deeper crisis with crucial internal reshuffles looming.
- Centre-right Diko fumes over the Anastassiades report. "The spirit of the report fully justifies our arguments to President Glafcos Clerides," says the junior coalition partner.
